trajectory_messages.content: [TextContent(type='text', text='{"message": "[\\"{\\\\\\"id\\\\\\":null,\\\\\\"metadata\\\\\\":{\\\\\\"id\\\\\\":\\\\\\"96f05359a5547949\\\\\\",\\\\\\"title\\\\\\":\\\\\\"Custom engine agents for Microsoft 365 overview\\\\\\",\\\\\\"heading\\\\\\":\\\\\\"Development approaches for custom engine agents - Pro-code approach\\\\\\",\\\\\\"doc_url\\\\\\":\\\\\\"https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/m365copilot-docs/blob/main/docs/overview-custom-engine-agent.md\\\\\\",\\\\\\"category\\\\\\":\\\\\\"docs\\\\\\"},\\\\\\"page_content\\\\\\":\\\\\\"For pro-code development, use Visual Studio or Visual Studio Code with the [Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit](https://aka.ms/M365AgentsToolkit) extension. This toolkit streamlines agent development by providing prebuilt templates, easy debugging, and streamlined deployment workflows. It\'s ideal for developers who want a fully customized experience.  \\\\\\\\nWhen building agents with the toolkit, choose between two SDKs depending on your needs.  \\\\\\\\n#### Microsoft 365 Agents SDK  \\\\\\\\nThe [Microsoft 365 Agents SDK](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/m365copilot-docs/blob/main/docs/create-deploy-agents-sdk.md) is a framework designed for building full-stack, multi-channel agents that can operate across Microsoft 365 Copilot, Teams, partner platforms, custom applications, and websites.  \\\\\\\\nIt\'s ideal for use cases that require custom orchestration using frameworks like Semantic Kernel or LangChain, and supports integration with any AI models or services. This SDK is best suited for organizations or ISVs that need highly tailored agents with advanced capabilities and the ability to operate across multiple channels.  \\\\\\\\n#### Teams SDK  \\\\\\\\nThe [Teams SDK](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/platform/teams-ai-library) is a framework tailored specifically for Microsoft Teams. It includes a built-in action planner orchestrator and supports GPT-based language models from Azure and OpenAI.  \\\\\\\\nThis option is ideal for organizations looking to build collaborative agents that operate within Teams channels and meetings. It\'s useful when building agents that interact in real time with users in a collaborative, team-based environment.\\\\\\",\\\\\\"type\\\\\\":\\\\\\"Document\\\\\\"}\\", \\"{\\\\\\"id\\\\\\":null,\\\\\\"metadata\\\\\\":{\\\\\\"id\\\\\\":\\\\\\"10c30b97c4b003ab\\\\\\",\\\\\\"title\\\\\\":\\\\\\"Create and deploy an agent with Microsoft 365 Agents SDK\\\\\\",\\\\\\"heading\\\\\\":\\\\\\"\\\\\\",\\\\\\"doc_url\\\\\\":\\\\\\"https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/m365copilot-docs/blob/main/docs/create-deploy-agents-sdk.md\\\\\\",\\\\\\"category\\\\\\":\\\\\\"docs\\\\\\"},\\\\\\"page_content\\\\\\":\\\\\\"The Microsoft 365 Agents SDK enables you to build custom engine agents by using the AI stack of your choice, then deploy them to Microsoft 365 Copilot. With the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit for Visual Studio and Visual Studio Code, you can use the built-in templates to scaffold your projects.  \\\\\\\\nThe SDK supports integration with a wide range of models and orchestrators\\\\u2014including Azure Foundry, Semantic Kernel, OpenAI Agents, LangChain, or custom-built solutions. You can even combine multiple agents built with different technologies and surface them through Microsoft 365 Copilot.\\\\\\",\\\\\\"type\\\\\\":\\\\\\"Document\\\\\\"}\\", \\"{\\\\\\"id\\\\\\":null,\\\\\\"metadata\\\\\\":{\\\\\\"id\\\\\\":\\\\\\"8fe82c6df20b94dc\\\\\\",\\\\\\"title\\\\\\":\\\\\\"Azure Bot Framework SDK to Agents SDK migration guidance\\\\\\",\\\\\\"heading\\\\\\":\\\\\\"\\\\\\",\\\\\\"doc_url\\\\\\":\\\\\\"https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/businessapps-copilot-docs-pr/blob/live/microsoft-365-agents/bf-migration-guidance.md\\\\\\",\\\\\\"category\\\\\\":\\\\\\"microsoft-365-agents\\\\\\"},\\\\\\"page_content\\\\\\":\\\\\\"The Microsoft 365 Agents SDK provides developers the ability to create and tailor agents using the AI stack of their choice. Developers can create a custom engine agent (CEA) and deploy it to Microsoft 365 Copilot. Developers can get started with the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit for Visual Studio and Visual Studio Code to get started quickly with scaffolding and templates. Developers can add their chosen models and orchestrator from Azure Foundry and Semantic Kernel, OpenAI Agents, LangChain, or even a custom built orchestrator. Developers can even  choose to bring multiple agents built with different technologies, and surface the agents through Microsoft 365 Copilot.  \\\\\\\\nUsing the Microsoft 365 Agents SDK, we want you to be able to build an agent quickly and surface it on any channel, including Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft Teams.  \\\\\\\\nThe Agents SDK is designed to be unopinionated about the AI you use. You can implement agentic patterns without being locked into a tech stack.  \\\\\\\\nThe Agents SDK takes advantage of specific client channel behavior, such as Microsoft 365 Copilot, Teams, and other non-Microsoft channels, to allow you to tailor your agent to client channels, including specific events or actions.\\\\\\",\\\\\\"type\\\\\\":\\\\\\"Document\\\\\\"}\\", \\"{\\\\\\"id\\\\\\":null,\\\\\\"metadata\\\\\\":{\\\\\\"id\\\\\\":\\\\\\"7f488fb4944aaece\\\\\\",\\\\\\"title\\\\\\":\\\\\\"Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit command line interface\\\\\\",\\\\\\"heading\\\\\\":\\\\\\"\\\\\\",\\\\\\"doc_url\\\\\\":\\\\\\"https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/msteams-docs/blob/live/msteams-platform/toolkit/Microsoft-365-Agents-Toolkit-CLI.md\\\\\\",\\\\\\"category\\\\\\":\\\\\\"msteams-platform/toolkit\\\\\\"},\\\\\\"page_content\\\\\\":\\\\\\">[!IMPORTANT]\\\\\\\\n>\\\\\\\\n> TeamsFx SDK is no longer supported by Microsoft for building Microsoft 365 Copilot extensions, Microsoft 365 agents, or modern Teams app scenarios. The SDK is currently in deprecation mode and will receive community-only support on GitHub until September 2026.\\\\\\\\n>\\\\\\\\n> For all new Microsoft-supported development (Copilot extensions, AI agents, Teams apps, or broader Microsoft 365 extensibility), use:\\\\\\\\n>\\\\\\\\n> - **[Microsoft 365 Agents SDK](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/agents-sdk/)** (recommended for all new Copilot or agent-based experiences)\\\\\\\\n> - **[Teams SDK](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/platform/teams-ai-library/welcome)** (for building Teams-only apps and bots)\\\\\\\\n>\\\\\\\\n> New projects should not be built with TeamsFx. Existing TeamsFx solutions should be migrated to the Microsoft 365 Agents SDK.  \\\\\\\\nMicrosoft 365 Agents Toolkit command line interface (Agents Toolkit CLI) is a text-based command line interface that can help scaffold, validate, and deploy applications for Microsoft 365 from the terminal or a CI/CD process. For more information, see [source code](https://github.com/OfficeDev/microsoft-365-agents-toolkit/tree/dev/packages/cli) and [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/m365agentstoolkit-cli).  \\\\\\\\nWhether you prefer keyboard-centric developer operations, or you are automating your CI/CD pipeline, Agents Toolkit CLI offers the same features as the IDE extensions. It provides the following features to facilitate the development of agents or apps for Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft Teams, and Microsoft 365:  \\\\\\\\n- **Collaboration**: Invite other developers to collaborate on your Agents Toolkit project to debug and deploy.\\\\\\\\n- **Agent/Application Creation**: Generate a new agent or app using available templates and samples.\\\\\\\\n- **Agent/Application Preview**: Upload and preview your agent or app in Teams, Outlook, and the Microsoft 365 app.\\\\\\",\\\\\\"type\\\\\\":\\\\\\"Document\\\\\\"}\\", \\"{\\\\\\"id\\\\\\":null,\\\\\\"metadata\\\\\\":{\\\\\\"id\\\\\\":\\\\\\"b969ee877d5211e5\\\\\\",\\\\\\"title\\\\\\":\\\\\\"Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit\\\\\\",\\\\\\"heading\\\\\\":\\\\\\"Deploy to multiple channels with Microsoft 365 Agents SDK\\\\\\",\\\\\\"doc_url\\\\\\":\\\\\\"https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/msteams-docs/blob/live/msteams-platform/toolkit/overview-agents-toolkit.md\\\\\\",\\\\\\"category\\\\\\":\\\\\\"msteams-platform/toolkit\\\\\\"},\\\\\\"page_content\\\\\\":\\\\\\"Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit has built-in support for [Microsoft 365 Agents SDK](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/agents-sdk/agents-sdk-overview), enabling you to build a custom engine agent and publish to multiple channels, including M365 Copilot, Microsoft Teams, Web, Email, SMS, and more. Alternately, you can build declarative agents that leverage the full power of the Microsoft 365 Copilot AI stack.  \\\\\\\\n![](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/msteams-docs/blob/live/msteams-platform/assets/images/agents-toolkit-landing/agents-channels.png)  \\\\\\\\nThe following video shows how easily you can get started building an agent with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit + Microsoft 365 Agents SDK:  \\\\\\\\n> [!VIDEO 4b7e966b-6874-4b68-a746-809dc091adae]  \\\\\\\\nOnce ready, you can use Agents Toolkit to easily [publish your agents](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365-copilot/extensibility/publish) and apps to the Microsoft Store, your organizational catalog, or for your own personal use.  \\\\\\\\n> [!div class=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"nextstepaction\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"]\\\\\\\\n> [Get started with Microsoft 365 Agents SDK and Agents Toolkit](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365-copilot/extensibility/create-deploy-agents-sdk)\\\\\\",\\\\\\"type\\\\\\":\\\\\\"Document\\\\\\"}\\", \\"{\\\\\\"id\\\\\\":null,\\\\\\"metadata\\\\\\":{\\\\\\"id\\\\\\":\\\\\\"5eb22d126517fd0b\\\\\\",\\\\\\"title\\\\\\":\\\\\\"Bring your agents into Microsoft 365 Copilot\\\\\\",\\\\\\"heading\\\\\\":\\\\\\"Use the Microsoft 365 Agents SDK\\\\\\",\\\\\\"doc_url\\\\\\":\\\\\\"https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/m365copilot-docs/blob/main/docs/bring-agents-to-copilot.md\\\\\\",\\\\\\"category\\\\\\":\\\\\\"docs\\\\\\"},\\\\\\"page_content\\\\\\":\\\\\\"To bring your agent into Microsoft 365 Copilot, use the [Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit](https://aka.ms/M365AgentsToolkit) to integrate the agent with the [Microsoft 365 Agents SDK](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/m365copilot-docs/blob/main/docs/m365-agents-sdk.md). The Agents SDK supports C#, JavaScript, and Python. If your agent is written in one of these languages, you don\'t have to modify it significantly. You can simply add the Agents SDK code to your agent and use the built-in channel adapters to deploy your agent to Microsoft 365 Copilot.  \\\\\\\\nThe built-in channel adapters in the Microsoft 365 Agents SDK support a number of channels, including Microsoft 365 Copilot.  By wrapping your existing agent with the Agents SDK, you can integrate with the Azure Bot Service that sits between a user surface or channel - such as Microsoft 365 Copilot - and your code. The Azure Bot Service translates what that channel sends and transforms it into common activities to match what your code understands-in this case, the Agents SDK wrapper that accepts incoming messages from Azure Bot Service.\\\\\\",\\\\\\"type\\\\\\":\\\\\\"Document\\\\\\"}\\", \\"{\\\\\\"id\\\\\\":null,\\\\\\"metadata\\\\\\":{\\\\\\"id\\\\\\":\\\\\\"2f5d032d5ce8b737\\\\\\",\\\\\\"title\\\\\\":\\\\\\"Choose the right tool to build your declarative agent\\\\\\",\\\\\\"heading\\\\\\":\\\\\\"Tools for building declarative agents\\\\\\",\\\\\\"doc_url\\\\\\":\\\\\\"https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/m365copilot-docs/blob/main/docs/declarative-agent-tool-comparison.md\\\\\\",\\\\\\"category\\\\\\":\\\\\\"docs\\\\\\"},\\\\\\"page_content\\\\\\":\\\\\\"Several tools are available to help you build declarative agents for Copilot. The following table lists the tools and the potential use cases for each to help you decide which tool is right for you.  \\\\\\\\n| **Tool** | **Coding approach** |**Description** | **Recommended use case** |\\\\\\\\n|:------------|:------------| :------------| :------------|\\\\\\\\n| [Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit](https://aka.ms/M365AgentsToolkit) | Pro-code | Agents Toolkit enables the creation of declarative agents with advanced features, such as custom API actions, adaptive cards, and CI/CD (Continuous Integration/Continuous Delivery) integration. | Developers who need full control over their coding environment, source |\\\\\\\\n| [Copilot Studio](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/microsoft-copilot-extend-copilot-extensions?context=/microsoft-365-copilot/extensibility/context) | Low-code | Copilot Studio allows users to create declarative agents using a drag-and-drop interface. It provides control over business logic and workflow automation and allows users to create declarative agents with advanced features, such as custom API actions, adaptive cards, and CI/CD integration. |  Information workers and business users who need a low-code, easy-to-use solution that includes [Power Platform integration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/developer/get-started). |\\\\\\",\\\\\\"type\\\\\\":\\\\\\"Document\\\\\\"}\\"]", "references": "\\n\\nCited References:\\n\\n\\n\\n- [Custom engine agents for Microsoft 365 overview - Development approaches for custom engine agents - Pro-code approach](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/m365copilot-docs/blob/main/docs/overview-custom-engine-agent.md#development-approaches-for-custom-engine-agents---pro-code-approach)\\n\\n- [Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit - Deploy to multiple channels with Microsoft 365 Agents SDK](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/msteams-docs/blob/live/msteams-platform/toolkit/overview-agents-toolkit.md#deploy-to-multiple-channels-with-microsoft-365-agents-sdk)\\n\\n- [Bring your agents into Microsoft 365 Copilot - Use the Microsoft 365 Agents SDK](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/m365copilot-docs/blob/main/docs/bring-agents-to-copilot.md#use-the-microsoft-365-agents-sdk)\\n\\n- [Choose the right tool to build your declarative agent - Tools for building declarative agents](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/m365copilot-docs/blob/main/docs/declarative-agent-tool-comparison.md#tools-for-building-declarative-agents)"}', annotations=None, meta=None)]

## **Core Components**

### **1. Microsoft 365 Copilot (Core Platform)**
- AI-powered productivity tool integrated with Microsoft 365 apps

- Can be extended through connectors, agents, and APIs

### **2. Extensibility Components**
- **Copilot Connectors**: Bring external data into Microsoft Graph for discovery across Microsoft 365 experiences
- **Power Platform Connectors**: Enable real-time interactions with external systems for read/write actions
- **Actions**: Define specific business behaviors using Power Platform components
- **Microsoft 365 Copilot APIs**: Provide secure programmatic access to Copilot capabilities

### **3. Agents (AI Assistant Components)**
- Specialized AI-powered assistants that automate workflows
- Two main types:
  - **Declarative Agents**: Use Copilot's AI infrastructure with custom instructions/knowledge/actions
  - **Custom Engine Agents**: Built with custom AI stacks (own models/orchestrators)

### **4. Development Tools & Frameworks**
- **Copilot Studio**: Low-code tool for building agents with drag-and-drop interface
- **Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit**: Pro-code tool for Visual Studio/VS Code with templates and CI/CD
- **Microsoft 365 Agents SDK**: Framework for building multi-channel agents with custom AI stacks
- **Teams SDK**: Framework specifically for Microsoft Teams agents
- **Azure AI**: Platform for AI services and models integration

## **Key Relationships**

### **Extension Pathways**
1. **Data Integration**: Copilot Connectors → enhance knowledge → Microsoft 365 Copilot
2. **Functionality Extension**: Actions → extend functionality → Microsoft 365 Copilot
3. **Capability Expansion**: Agents → extend capabilities → Microsoft 365 Copilot

### **Agent Development**
1. **Declarative Agents** can be built using:
   - Copilot Studio (low-code)
   - Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit (pro-code)
   
2. **Custom Engine Agents** require:
   - Microsoft 365 Agents SDK
   - Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit

### **Tool Relationships**
- Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit **uses** Microsoft 365 Agents SDK
- Copilot Studio **manages governance** of Power Platform Connectors
- Microsoft 365 Agents SDK **integrates with** Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit

### **Component Integration**
- Power Platform Connectors **enable interactions** for Agents
- Copilot Connectors **provide custom knowledge** for Declarative Agents
- Actions **can be added to** Agents
- Microsoft 365 Copilot APIs **integrate with** Custom Engine Agents

## **Development Approaches**

| Approach | Tools | Best For |
|----------|-------|----------|
| **Low-code** | Copilot Studio | Business users, quick prototyping |
| **Pro-code** | Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit + SDK | Developers needing full control |
| **Teams-focused** | Teams SDK | Collaborative agents within Teams |
| **Custom AI** | Agents SDK + Azure AI | Advanced AI integration needs |

answer:
Based on your notes about JWT implementation and authentication workflows, I've created a comprehensive onboarding document for new developers. Here's a structured guide covering your API authentication system:

# API Authentication Workflow - Developer Onboarding Guide

## Overview
This document provides new developers with a complete understanding of our API authentication system, focusing on JWT implementation, security practices, and integration patterns used across our applications.

## 1. Authentication Architecture

### 1.1 System Components
Our authentication system consists of three main layers:

1. **Client Layer**: Web applications (Next.js) and mobile apps
2. **Gateway Layer**: API Gateway with JWT validation
3. **Service Layer**: Microservices with role-based authorization

### 1.2 Authentication Flow
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Gateway
    participant AuthService
    participant BackendService
    
    Client->>Gateway: Request with credentials
    Gateway->>AuthService: Validate credentials
    AuthService->>Gateway: Return JWT token
    Gateway->>Client: Set secure cookie with JWT
    
    Note over Client,Gateway: Subsequent requests
    
    Client->>Gateway: Request with JWT cookie
    Gateway->>Gateway: Validate JWT signature
    Gateway->>BackendService: Forward request with user context
    BackendService->>Gateway: Process request
    Gateway->>Client: Return response
```

## 2. JWT Implementation Details

### 2.1 Token Structure
We use HS256 (HMAC with SHA-256) algorithm for JWT tokens with the following structure:

```json
{
  "header": {
    "alg": "HS256",
    "typ": "JWT"
  },
  "payload": {
    "userId": "user_123",
    "role": "developer",
    "iat": 1678901234,
    "exp": 1679506034,
    "iss": "our-api-gateway"
  },
  "signature": "HMAC_SHA256(base64UrlEncode(header) + '.' + base64UrlEncode(payload), secret)"
}
```

### 2.2 Token Generation (Next.js Example)
Based on your notes, here's our JWT implementation using the `jose` library:

```typescript
// /app/lib/session.ts
import 'server-only'
import { SignJWT, jwtVerify } from 'jose'

const secretKey = process.env.SESSION_SECRET
const encodedKey = new TextEncoder().encode(secretKey)

export async function encrypt(payload: any) {
  return new SignJWT(payload)
    .setProtectedHeader({ alg: 'HS256' })
    .setIssuedAt()
    .setExpirationTime('7d')
    .sign(encodedKey)
}

export async function decrypt(session: string | undefined = '') {
  try {
    const { payload } = await jwtVerify(session, encodedKey, {
      algorithms: ['HS256'],
    })
    return payload
  } catch (error) {
    console.log('Failed to verify session')
    return null
  }
}
```

### 2.3 Secure Cookie Configuration
```typescript
export async function createSession(userId: string) {
  const expiresAt = new Date(Date.now() + 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000)
  const session = await encrypt({ userId, expiresAt })
  const cookieStore = await cookies()

  cookieStore.set('session', session, {
    httpOnly: true,    // Prevent client-side JavaScript access
    secure: true,      // Only send over HTTPS
    expires: expiresAt,
    sameSite: 'lax',   // CSRF protection
    path: '/',
  })
}
```

## 3. API Gateway Authentication

### 3.1 Gateway Security Layer
The API Gateway handles initial authentication with these components:

- **JWT Validation**: Verifies token signature and expiration
- **Rate Limiting**: 5 requests per minute for `/login` endpoints
- **IP Filtering**: Whitelist/blacklist management
- **Request Logging**: Structured logging for security auditing

### 3.2 Request Flow
1. **Client Request** → HTTP/HTTPS request arrives
2. **Security Validation** → JWT verification (if present)
3. **Rate Limiting** → Check request frequency
4. **Routing Decision** → Route to appropriate service
5. **Service Invocation** → Forward with user context
6. **Response Processing** → Add security headers

## 4. Security Best Practices

### 4.1 Password Security
```python
# From Flask Modernization Plan
import bcrypt

def hash_password(password):
    salt = bcrypt.gensalt()
    return bcrypt.hashpw(password.encode(), salt)

def verify_password(password, hashed):
    return bcrypt.checkpw(password.encode(), hashed)
```

### 4.2 Session Security Configuration
```python
# Flask session configuration
app.config.update(
    SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY=True,
    SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=True,
    SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE='Lax',
    PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME=timedelta(hours=1)
)
```

### 4.3 Security Headers
All responses include these security headers:
- `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`
- `X-Frame-Options: DENY`
- `X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block`
- `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains`

## 5. Developer Workflows

### 5.1 Implementing Login Endpoint
```typescript
// Next.js API route example
import type { NextApiRequest, NextApiResponse } from 'next'
import { createSession } from '@/app/lib/session'
import { verifyCredentials } from '@/app/lib/auth'

export default async function handler(
  req: NextApiRequest,
  res: NextApiResponse
) {
  try {
    const { email, password } = req.body
    
    // Verify credentials
    const user = await verifyCredentials(email, password)
    if (!user) {
      return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Invalid credentials' })
    }
    
    // Create session
    await createSession(user.id)
    
    res.status(200).json({ success: true, user: { id: user.id, email: user.email } })
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Login error:', error)
    res.status(500).json({ error: 'Internal server error' })
  }
}
```

### 5.2 Protecting API Routes
```typescript
// Middleware for protected routes
import 'server-only'
import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
import { decrypt } from '@/app/lib/session'
import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'

export const verifySession = cache(async () => {
  const cookie = cookies().get('session')?.value
  const session = await decrypt(cookie)

  if (!session?.userId) {
    redirect('/login')
  }

  return { isAuth: true, userId: session.userId }
})

// Usage in server components
export default async function ProtectedPage() {
  const { userId } = await verifySession()
  // ... rest of component
}
```

### 5.3 Rate Limiting Implementation
```python
# Flask rate limiting example
from flask_limiter import Limiter
from flask_limiter.util import get_remote_address

limiter = Limiter(get_remote_address, app=app)

@app.route('/login', methods=['POST'])
@limiter.limit("5 per minute")
def login():
    # Login logic
    pass
```

## 6. Environment Configuration

### 6.1 Required Environment Variables
```bash
# .env.local (Next.js)
SESSION_SECRET="your-256-bit-secret-key-here"
DATABASE_URL="postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/db"
NEXTAUTH_URL="http://localhost:3000"
NEXTAUTH_SECRET="your-nextauth-secret"

# Flask application
SECRET_KEY="your-flask-secret-key"
SESSION_SECRET="your-session-secret"
BCRYPT_LOG_ROUNDS=12
```

### 6.2 Secret Management
- **Never commit secrets** to version control
- Use environment variables or secret management services
- Rotate secrets regularly (every 90 days)
- Use different secrets for development, staging, production

## 7. Testing Authentication

### 7.1 Unit Test Examples
```typescript
// Testing session creation
import { encrypt, decrypt } from '@/app/lib/session'

describe('Session Management', () => {
  beforeAll(() => {
    process.env.SESSION_SECRET = 'test-secret'
  })

  test('encrypt and decrypt session', async () => {
    const payload = { userId: 'test-123', role: 'admin' }
    const token = await encrypt(payload)
    const decoded = await decrypt(token)
    
    expect(decoded.userId).toBe(payload.userId)
    expect(decoded.role).toBe(payload.role)
  })
})
```

### 7.2 Integration Test Example
```python
# Flask authentication test
def test_login_rate_limiting(client):
    # Test rate limiting
    for i in range(5):
        response = client.post('/login', data={
            'email': 'test@example.com',
            'password': 'wrongpassword'
        })
        assert response.status_code == 401
    
    # 6th attempt should be rate limited
    response = client.post('/login', data={
        'email': 'test@example.com',
        'password': 'wrongpassword'
    })
    assert response.status_code == 429  # Too Many Requests
```

## 8. Common Tasks for Developers

### 8.1 Adding New Protected Route
1. Create API route or page component
2. Import and use `verifySession()` middleware
3. Add role-based checks if needed
4. Test with valid and invalid sessions

### 8.2 Debugging Authentication Issues
1. **Check cookies**: Verify `session` cookie is present and secure
2. **Validate JWT**: Use [jwt.io](https://jwt.io) to decode token
3. **Check expiration**: Ensure token hasn't expired
4. **Verify secret**: Confirm `SESSION_SECRET` matches between services
5. **Review logs**: Check structured logs for authentication events

### 8.3 Rotating Secrets
1. Generate new secret key
2. Update environment variables
3. Restart services (users will need to re-authenticate)
4. Monitor for authentication failures

## 9. Security Incident Response

### 9.1 Immediate Actions
If you suspect a security breach:

1. **Reset sessions**: Invalidate all active sessions
2. **Rotate secrets**: Change all authentication secrets
3. **Review logs**: Check for suspicious activity patterns
4. **Enable enhanced logging**: Capture detailed authentication events

### 9.2 Reporting Issues
- Use internal security channel for reporting
- Include: timestamp, user ID, IP address, request details
- Do not share sensitive information in public channels

## 10. Additional Resources

### 10.1 Internal Documentation
- [Next.js Authentication Guide](/markdown/next.js-authentication-guide)
- [API Gateway Architecture](/docs/api-gateway-architecture-technical-specs)
- [Flask Modernization Plan](/markdown/flask-authentication-app-modernization-plan)

### 10.2 External References
- [JWT Introduction](https://jwt.io/introduction)
- [OWASP Authentication Cheatsheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authentication_Cheat_Sheet.html)
- [Next.js Auth Documentation](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/authentication)

### 10.3 Tools & Libraries
- **jose**: JWT implementation library
- **bcrypt**: Password hashing
- **flask-limiter**: Rate limiting for Flask
- **structlog**: Structured logging

# API Gateway Architecture Technical Specifications

## Overview
The API Gateway serves as a single entry point for all client requests to our microservices ecosystem. It handles request routing, composition, and protocol translation, providing a unified API to clients while abstracting the underlying microservices architecture.

## Core Components

### 1. Gateway Core
- **Request Router**: Routes incoming requests to appropriate microservices based on path, method, and headers
- **Protocol Translator**: Handles HTTP/HTTPS, WebSocket, and gRPC protocols
- **Load Balancer**: Distributes traffic across service instances using round-robin, least connections, or consistent hashing algorithms

### 2. Security Layer
- **Authentication**: JWT validation, OAuth 2.0 token verification
- **Authorization**: Role-based access control (RBAC), policy enforcement
- **Rate Limiting**: Per-IP, per-user, and per-API key rate limiting
- **IP Whitelisting/Blacklisting**: Network-level access control

### 3. Transformation Engine
- **Request/Response Transformation**: JSON/XML conversion, field mapping, format adaptation
- **Protocol Bridging**: REST to gRPC, SOAP to REST conversions
- **Payload Compression**: Gzip, Brotli compression for response optimization

### 4. Monitoring & Analytics
- **Request Logging**: Structured logging of all incoming/outgoing traffic
- **Metrics Collection**: Latency, error rates, throughput metrics
- **Distributed Tracing**: Correlation IDs for end-to-end request tracking

## Architecture Diagram

```mermaid
graph TD
    Client[Client Applications] --> Gateway[API Gateway]
    
    Gateway --> Auth[Authentication Service]
    Gateway --> User[User Service]
    Gateway --> Product[Product Service]
    Gateway --> Order[Order Service]
    Gateway --> Payment[Payment Service]
    
    subgraph "Microservices Layer"
        Auth
        User
        Product
        Order
        Payment
    end
    
    Auth --> DB1[(Auth Database)]
    User --> DB2[(User Database)]
    Product --> DB3[(Product Database)]
    Order --> DB4[(Order Database)]
    Payment --> DB5[(Payment Database)]
```

## Request Flow

1. **Client Request**: HTTP/HTTPS request arrives at gateway
2. **Security Validation**: Authentication & authorization checks
3. **Rate Limiting**: Check if request is within allowed limits
4. **Routing Decision**: Determine target microservice based on URL path and headers
5. **Protocol Translation**: Convert request format if needed
6. **Service Invocation**: Forward request to appropriate microservice
7. **Response Processing**: Transform response, add headers, compress if needed
8. **Client Response**: Return formatted response to client

## Performance Requirements

- **Latency**: < 50ms added latency for gateway processing
- **Throughput**: Support up to 10,000 requests per second
- **Availability**: 99.99% uptime SLA
- **Scalability**: Horizontal scaling with auto-scaling based on CPU/memory metrics

## Deployment Architecture

- **Primary Region**: Active-active deployment across 3 availability zones
- **Disaster Recovery**: Warm standby in secondary region with 5-minute RPO
- **CDN Integration**: CloudFront/Akamai integration for static content caching
- **WAF Integration**: Web Application Firewall for DDoS protection

## Monitoring & Alerting

- **Key Metrics**: Request rate, error rate (4xx, 5xx), latency (p50, p95, p99)
- **Alerting**: PagerDuty integration for critical alerts
- **Dashboards**: Real-time monitoring dashboards in Grafana
- **Log Aggregation**: Centralized logging via ELK stack

## Security Considerations

- **TLS Termination**: SSL/TLS termination at gateway with certificate rotation
- **API Key Management**: Secure storage and rotation of API keys
- **Secrets Management**: Integration with HashiCorp Vault or AWS Secrets Manager
- **Vulnerability Scanning**: Regular security scans and penetration testing

## Versioning Strategy

- **URL Path Versioning**: `/v1/`, `/v2/` in URL paths
- **Header Versioning**: `Accept-Version` header for version negotiation
- **Deprecation Policy**: 6-month deprecation period with migration guides
- **Backward Compatibility**: Maintain backward compatibility for at least 2 major versions

## Development Roadmap

### Phase 1 (Current)
- Basic routing and load balancing
- JWT authentication
- Rate limiting per API key

### Phase 2 (Q2 2026)
- Advanced transformation engine
- gRPC protocol support
- Distributed tracing integration

### Phase 3 (Q3 2026)
- GraphQL federation
- WebSocket support
- Advanced caching strategies

## Team Responsibilities

- **Platform Team**: Gateway infrastructure and core functionality
- **Security Team**: Security policies and compliance
- **Product Teams**: API design and microservice integration
- **SRE Team**: Deployment, monitoring, and incident response', annotations=None, meta=None)]

# Flask Authentication Application Modernization Plan

## Executive Summary
This document outlines a comprehensive modernization plan for an outdated Python Flask authentication application that has not been updated in 3 years. The plan addresses technical debt, security vulnerabilities, dependency management, and architectural improvements.

## 1. Technical Debt Assessment

### 1.1 Dependency Analysis
- **Outdated Flask ecosystem**: Likely using Flask <2.0, Flask-Login <0.5, Flask-WTF <0.15
- **Deprecated Python version**: Possibly Python 3.6 or 3.7 (end-of-life)
- **Vulnerable dependencies**: Libraries with known CVEs from 3+ years ago
- **Missing security updates**: No recent patches for critical vulnerabilities

### 1.2 Code Quality Issues
- **Monolithic structure**: Lack of modularization and separation of concerns
- **Poor error handling**: Inconsistent exception handling and error reporting
- **Minimal testing**: Likely inadequate test coverage, especially for security features
- **Hardcoded configuration**: Secrets embedded in source code
- **Lack of documentation**: Missing API documentation and code comments

### 1.3 Architectural Concerns
- **Direct SQL queries**: Instead of using ORM or query builders
- **Synchronous operations**: No async support for modern performance
- **Basic session management**: Potentially insecure session handling
- **No API versioning**: Makes future updates difficult
- **Minimal logging**: Insufficient audit trails for security events

## 2. Security Vulnerability Assessment

### 2.1 Critical Vulnerabilities (Immediate Action Required)

#### 2.1.1 Authentication & Authorization
- **Weak password hashing**: Potential use of MD5, SHA1, or unsalted hashes
- **Missing CSRF protection**: No Flask-WTF or CSRF tokens in forms
- **Insecure session cookies**: Missing HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite flags
- **No rate limiting**: Brute-force attacks possible on login endpoints
- **Insecure direct object references**: Users may access other users' data

#### 2.1.2 Injection Vulnerabilities
- **SQL injection**: String concatenation in SQL queries
- **XSS vulnerabilities**: Unescaped user input in templates
- **Command injection**: Use of `os.system()` or `subprocess` with user input

#### 2.1.3 Data Protection
- **Plaintext secrets**: Passwords, API keys in configuration files
- **Insufficient encryption**: Weak or no encryption for sensitive data
- **Information leakage**: Detailed error messages exposing system details

### 2.2 High Severity Issues

#### 2.2.1 Dependency Security
- **Known CVEs**: Outdated libraries with published exploits
- **Unmaintained packages**: Dependencies with no recent updates
- **Supply chain risks**: No dependency scanning or verification

#### 2.2.2 Configuration Security
- **Development settings in production**: Debug mode enabled, verbose errors
- **Weak secret keys**: Default or short SECRET_KEY values
- **Missing security headers**: No CSP, HSTS, or X-Frame-Options

### 2.3 Medium Severity Issues
- **Insecure password policies**: No complexity requirements or expiration
- **Missing MFA support**: No two-factor authentication options
- **Inadequate logging**: Security events not captured or monitored
- **No input validation**: Lack of schema validation for API endpoints

## 3. Modernization Plan

### Phase 1: Foundation & Security (Weeks 1-2)

#### 3.1.1 Dependency Updates
1. **Upgrade Python**: Migrate to Python 3.11+ (LTS version)
2. **Update Flask ecosystem**:
   - Flask → 3.0.x
   - Flask-Login → 0.6.x
   - Flask-WTF → 1.2.x
   - Flask-SQLAlchemy → 3.1.x
3. **Add security dependencies**:
   - `bcrypt` for password hashing
   - `cryptography` for encryption
   - `python-dotenv` for configuration management
   - `bleach` for input sanitization

#### 3.1.2 Security Hardening
1. **Implement password security**:
   ```python
   # Replace with bcrypt
   from werkzeug.security import generate_password_hash, check_password_hash
   # Change to:
   import bcrypt
   
   def hash_password(password):
       salt = bcrypt.gensalt()
       return bcrypt.hashpw(password.encode(), salt)
   ```

2. **Secure session configuration**:
   ```python
   app.config.update(
       SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY=True,
       SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=True,
       SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE='Lax',
       PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME=timedelta(hours=1)
   )
   ```

3. **Add CSRF protection**:
   ```python
   from flask_wtf.csrf import CSRFProtect
   csrf = CSRFProtect(app)
   ```

4. **Implement rate limiting**:
   ```python
   from flask_limiter import Limiter
   from flask_limiter.util import get_remote_address
   
   limiter = Limiter(get_remote_address, app=app)
   
   @app.route('/login', methods=['POST'])
   @limiter.limit("5 per minute")
   def login():
       # login logic
   ```

### Phase 2: Code Refactoring (Weeks 3-4)

#### 3.2.1 Architecture Improvements
1. **Adopt application factory pattern**:
   ```python
   def create_app(config=None):
       app = Flask(__name__)
       if config:
           app.config.from_object(config)
       # Initialize extensions
       db.init_app(app)
       login_manager.init_app(app)
       return app
   ```

2. **Implement Blueprints for modularization**:
   ```python
   # auth/__init__.py
   from flask import Blueprint
   
   auth_bp = Blueprint('auth', __name__)
   
   @auth_bp.route('/login')
   def login():
       pass
   
   # app.py
   from auth import auth_bp
   app.register_blueprint(auth_bp, url_prefix='/auth')
   ```

3. **Add data layer abstraction**:
   - Replace raw SQL with SQLAlchemy ORM
   - Implement repository pattern for data access
   - Add migration support with Flask-Migrate

#### 3.2.2 Error Handling & Logging
1. **Centralized error handling**:
   ```python
   @app.errorhandler(404)
   def not_found(error):
       return jsonify({'error': 'Not found'}), 404
   
   @app.errorhandler(500)
   def internal_error(error):
       # Log error but don't expose details
       app.logger.error(f'Internal error: {error}')
       return jsonify({'error': 'Internal server error'}), 500
   ```

2. **Structured logging**:
   ```python
   import structlog
   
   logger = structlog.get_logger()
   
   def audit_log(user_id, action, status):
       logger.info("security_event",
                   user_id=user_id,
                   action=action,
                   status=status,
                   timestamp=datetime.utcnow())
   ```

### Phase 3: Advanced Features & Testing (Weeks 5-6)

#### 3.3.1 Enhanced Security Features
1. **Add multi-factor authentication**:
   - Implement TOTP-based 2FA
   - Support backup codes
   - Add recovery mechanisms

2. **API security improvements**:
   - Implement JWT tokens for stateless authentication
   - Add API key management
   - Implement request signing

3. **Security headers**:
   ```python
   @app.after_request
   def add_security_headers(response):
       response.headers['X-Content-Type-Options'] = 'nosniff'
       response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = 'DENY'
       response.headers['X-XSS-Protection'] = '1; mode=block'
       response.headers['Strict-Transport-Security'] = 'max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains'
       return response
   ```

#### 3.3.2 Testing Strategy
1. **Security testing**:
   - Unit tests for authentication logic
   - Integration tests for security controls
   - Penetration testing with OWASP ZAP

2. **Automated vulnerability scanning**:
   ```yaml
   # GitHub Actions workflow
   name: Security Scan
   on: [push, pull_request]
   jobs:
     security:
       runs-on: ubuntu-latest
       steps:
         - uses: actions/checkout@v4
         - name: Run bandit
           run: pip install bandit && bandit -r .
         - name: Run safety check
           run: pip install safety && safety check
   ```

3. **Dependency monitoring**:
   - Configure Dependabot or Renovate
   - Regular security updates
   - CVE alerting

### Phase 4: Deployment & Monitoring (Weeks 7-8)

#### 3.4.1 Deployment Improvements
1. **Containerization**:
   ```dockerfile
   FROM python:3.11-slim
   WORKDIR /app
   COPY requirements.txt .
   RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
   COPY . .
   USER nonroot
   CMD ["gunicorn", "wsgi:app", "--bind", "0.0.0.0:8000"]
   ```

2. **Environment configuration**:
   - Use 12-factor app principles
   - Externalize all configuration
   - Secrets management with HashiCorp Vault or AWS Secrets Manager

3. **CI/CD pipeline**:
   - Automated testing and security scanning
   - Container image scanning with Trivy
   - Deployment to staging with canary releases

#### 3.4.2 Monitoring & Observability
1. **Metrics collection**:
   - Authentication success/failure rates
   - API endpoint response times
   - Error rates by endpoint

2. **Security monitoring**:
   - Failed login attempts
   - Suspicious activity detection
   - Audit log aggregation

3. **Alerting**:
   - Real-time alerts for security incidents
   - Daily security summary reports
   - Monthly compliance reports

## 4. Risk Mitigation Strategy

### 4.1 Immediate Actions (First 48 hours)
1. **Disable vulnerable endpoints**: If critical vulnerabilities found
2. **Add WAF rules**: Temporary protection while fixing
3. **Enable enhanced logging**: Capture all authentication attempts
4. **Reset user sessions**: If session security compromised

### 4.2 Short-term Measures (Week 1)
1. **Update critical dependencies**: Fix known CVEs
2. **Implement basic rate limiting**: Prevent brute-force attacks
3. **Add security headers**: Quick win for web security
4. **Review and rotate secrets**: All passwords, keys, tokens

### 4.3 Long-term Improvements
1. **Regular security audits**: Quarterly penetration testing
2. **Security training**: Developer security awareness
3. **Bug bounty program**: Incentivize responsible disclosure
4. **Compliance certification**: SOC 2, ISO 27001

## 5. Success Metrics

### 5.1 Security Metrics
- Zero critical vulnerabilities in dependency scans
- 100% of passwords using bcrypt with proper salts
- All API endpoints with rate limiting
- Security headers score of A+ on securityheaders.com

### 5.2 Code Quality Metrics
- Test coverage >80% for authentication modules
- Static analysis with zero high-severity findings
- All dependencies updated within 30 days of release
- Documentation coverage for all public APIs

### 5.3 Performance Metrics
- Login response time <200ms at p95
- Authentication API availability >99.9%
- Session management overhead <5ms

## 6. Rollback Plan

### 6.1 Pre-deployment
1. **Backup current system**: Database, configuration, code
2. **Document current state**: Version numbers, configurations
3. **Prepare rollback scripts**: Automated revert procedures

### 6.2 Deployment strategy
1. **Canary deployment**: 5% → 25% → 50% → 100%
2. **Feature flags**: Gradual enablement of new features
3. **A/B testing**: Compare old vs new authentication flows

### 6.3 Rollback triggers
1. **Security incidents**: Any breach or vulnerability discovery
2. **Performance degradation**: Response time increase >50%
3. **User impact**: Login failure rate >1%
4. **System instability**: Error rate >5%

## 7. Maintenance Plan

### 7.1 Regular Activities
- **Weekly**: Dependency updates, security scan review
- **Monthly**: Security audit, penetration testing
- **Quarterly**: Architecture review, threat modeling
- **Annually**: Full security assessment, compliance review

### 7.2 Documentation
- Keep architecture diagrams updated
- Maintain security incident response plan
- Document all security decisions and trade-offs
- Update runbooks for operational procedures

## 8. Conclusion

This modernization plan provides a structured approach to addressing technical debt and security vulnerabilities in the outdated Flask authentication application. By following this phased approach, we can systematically improve security, maintainability, and performance while minimizing disruption to users.

**Next Steps**:
1. Conduct a detailed code review to identify specific vulnerabilities
2. Create a prioritized backlog of security fixes
3. Establish a cross-functional modernization team
4. Begin Phase 1 implementation immediately

---

# API Authentication Workflow - Developer Onboarding Guide

## Overview
This document provides new developers with a complete understanding of our API authentication system, focusing on JWT implementation, security practices, and integration patterns used across our applications.

## 1. Authentication Architecture

### 1.1 System Components
Our authentication system consists of three main layers:

1. **Client Layer**: Web applications (Next.js) and mobile apps
2. **Gateway Layer**: API Gateway with JWT validation
3. **Service Layer**: Microservices with role-based authorization

### 1.2 Authentication Flow
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Gateway
    participant AuthService
    participant BackendService
    
    Client->>Gateway: Request with credentials
    Gateway->>AuthService: Validate credentials
    AuthService->>Gateway: Return JWT token
    Gateway->>Client: Set secure cookie with JWT
    
    Note over Client,Gateway: Subsequent requests
    
    Client->>Gateway: Request with JWT cookie
    Gateway->>Gateway: Validate JWT signature
    Gateway->>BackendService: Forward request with user context
    BackendService->>Gateway: Process request
    Gateway->>Client: Return response
```

## 2. JWT Implementation Details

### 2.1 Token Structure
We use HS256 (HMAC with SHA-256) algorithm for JWT tokens with the following structure:

```json
{
  "header": {
    "alg": "HS256",
    "typ": "JWT"
  },
  "payload": {
    "userId": "user_123",
    "role": "developer",
    "iat": 1678901234,
    "exp": 1679506034,
    "iss": "our-api-gateway"
  },
  "signature": "HMAC_SHA256(base64UrlEncode(header) + '.' + base64UrlEncode(payload), secret)"
}
```

### 2.2 Token Generation (Next.js Example)
Based on your notes, here's our JWT implementation using the `jose` library:

```typescript
// /app/lib/session.ts
import 'server-only'
import { SignJWT, jwtVerify } from 'jose'

const secretKey = process.env.SESSION_SECRET
const encodedKey = new TextEncoder().encode(secretKey)

export async function encrypt(payload: any) {
  return new SignJWT(payload)
    .setProtectedHeader({ alg: 'HS256' })
    .setIssuedAt()
    .setExpirationTime('7d')
    .sign(encodedKey)
}

export async function decrypt(session: string | undefined = '') {
  try {
    const { payload } = await jwtVerify(session, encodedKey, {
      algorithms: ['HS256'],
    })
    return payload
  } catch (error) {
    console.log('Failed to verify session')
    return null
  }
}
```

### 2.3 Secure Cookie Configuration
```typescript
export async function createSession(userId: string) {
  const expiresAt = new Date(Date.now() + 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000)
  const session = await encrypt({ userId, expiresAt })
  const cookieStore = await cookies()

  cookieStore.set('session', session, {
    httpOnly: true,    // Prevent client-side JavaScript access
    secure: true,      // Only send over HTTPS
    expires: expiresAt,
    sameSite: 'lax',   // CSRF protection
    path: '/',
  })
}
```

## 3. API Gateway Authentication

### 3.1 Gateway Security Layer
The API Gateway handles initial authentication with these components:

- **JWT Validation**: Verifies token signature and expiration
- **Rate Limiting**: 5 requests per minute for `/login` endpoints
- **IP Filtering**: Whitelist/blacklist management
- **Request Logging**: Structured logging for security auditing

### 3.2 Request Flow
1. **Client Request** → HTTP/HTTPS request arrives
2. **Security Validation** → JWT verification (if present)
3. **Rate Limiting** → Check request frequency
4. **Routing Decision** → Route to appropriate service
5. **Service Invocation** → Forward with user context
6. **Response Processing** → Add security headers

## 4. Security Best Practices

### 4.1 Password Security
```python
# From Flask Modernization Plan
import bcrypt

def hash_password(password):
    salt = bcrypt.gensalt()
    return bcrypt.hashpw(password.encode(), salt)

def verify_password(password, hashed):
    return bcrypt.checkpw(password.encode(), hashed)
```

### 4.2 Session Security Configuration
```python
# Flask session configuration
app.config.update(
    SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY=True,
    SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=True,
    SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE='Lax',
    PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME=timedelta(hours=1)
)
```

### 4.3 Security Headers
All responses include these security headers:
- `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`
- `X-Frame-Options: DENY`
- `X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block`
- `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains`

## 5. Developer Workflows

### 5.1 Implementing Login Endpoint
```typescript
// Next.js API route example
import type { NextApiRequest, NextApiResponse } from 'next'
import { createSession } from '@/app/lib/session'
import { verifyCredentials } from '@/app/lib/auth'

export default async function handler(
  req: NextApiRequest,
  res: NextApiResponse
) {
  try {
    const { email, password } = req.body
    
    // Verify credentials
    const user = await verifyCredentials(email, password)
    if (!user) {
      return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Invalid credentials' })
    }
    
    // Create session
    await createSession(user.id)
    
    res.status(200).json({ success: true, user: { id: user.id, email: user.email } })
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Login error:', error)
    res.status(500).json({ error: 'Internal server error' })
  }
}
```

### 5.2 Protecting API Routes
```typescript
// Middleware for protected routes
import 'server-only'
import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
import { decrypt } from '@/app/lib/session'
import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'

export const verifySession = cache(async () => {
  const cookie = cookies().get('session')?.value
  const session = await decrypt(cookie)

  if (!session?.userId) {
    redirect('/login')
  }

  return { isAuth: true, userId: session.userId }
})

// Usage in server components
export default async function ProtectedPage() {
  const { userId } = await verifySession()
  // ... rest of component
}
```

### 5.3 Rate Limiting Implementation
```python
# Flask rate limiting example
from flask_limiter import Limiter
from flask_limiter.util import get_remote_address

limiter = Limiter(get_remote_address, app=app)

@app.route('/login', methods=['POST'])
@limiter.limit("5 per minute")
def login():
    # Login logic
    pass
```

## 6. Environment Configuration

### 6.1 Required Environment Variables
```bash
# .env.local (Next.js)
SESSION_SECRET="your-256-bit-secret-key-here"
DATABASE_URL="postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/db"
NEXTAUTH_URL="http://localhost:3000"
NEXTAUTH_SECRET="your-nextauth-secret"

# Flask application
SECRET_KEY="your-flask-secret-key"
SESSION_SECRET="your-session-secret"
BCRYPT_LOG_ROUNDS=12
```

### 6.2 Secret Management
- **Never commit secrets** to version control
- Use environment variables or secret management services
- Rotate secrets regularly (every 90 days)
- Use different secrets for development, staging, production

## 7. Testing Authentication

### 7.1 Unit Test Examples
```typescript
// Testing session creation
import { encrypt, decrypt } from '@/app/lib/session'

describe('Session Management', () => {
  beforeAll(() => {
    process.env.SESSION_SECRET = 'test-secret'
  })

  test('encrypt and decrypt session', async () => {
    const payload = { userId: 'test-123', role: 'admin' }
    const token = await encrypt(payload)
    const decoded = await decrypt(token)
    
    expect(decoded.userId).toBe(payload.userId)
    expect(decoded.role).toBe(payload.role)
  })
})
```

### 7.2 Integration Test Example
```python
# Flask authentication test
def test_login_rate_limiting(client):
    # Test rate limiting
    for i in range(5):
        response = client.post('/login', data={
            'email': 'test@example.com',
            'password': 'wrongpassword'
        })
        assert response.status_code == 401
    
    # 6th attempt should be rate limited
    response = client.post('/login', data={
        'email': 'test@example.com',
        'password': 'wrongpassword'
    })
    assert response.status_code == 429  # Too Many Requests
```

## 8. Common Tasks for Developers

### 8.1 Adding New Protected Route
1. Create API route or page component
2. Import and use `verifySession()` middleware
3. Add role-based checks if needed
4. Test with valid and invalid sessions

### 8.2 Debugging Authentication Issues
1. **Check cookies**: Verify `session` cookie is present and secure
2. **Validate JWT**: Use [jwt.io](https://jwt.io) to decode token
3. **Check expiration**: Ensure token hasn't expired
4. **Verify secret**: Confirm `SESSION_SECRET` matches between services

### 8.3 Rotating Secrets

2. Update environment variables
3. Restart services (users will need to re-authenticate)
4. Monitor for authentication failures

## 9. Security Incident Response

### 9.1 Immediate Actions
If you suspect a security breach:

1. **Reset sessions**: Invalidate all active sessions
2. **Rotate secrets**: Change all authentication secrets

{"title": "AI Agents for Document Summarization - Research Notes", "content": "# AI Agents for Document Summarization - Research Notes

## Overview
Document summarization is a critical NLP task that involves condensing lengthy documents into concise summaries while preserving key information. AI agents specializing in this domain can automate and enhance this process for various applications.

## Types of Document Summarization Agents

### 1. **Extractive Summarization Agents**
- **Approach**: Select and combine important sentences/phrases from the original document
- **Key Techniques**: TextRank, LexRank, BERT-based extraction
- **Use Cases**: News articles, legal documents, research papers
- **Strengths**: Preserves original wording, maintains factual accuracy
- **Limitations**: May produce less coherent summaries

### 2. **Abstractive Summarization Agents**
- **Approach**: Generate new sentences that capture the essence of the original
- **Key Techniques**: Transformer models (T5, BART, PEGASUS), Sequence-to-sequence models
- **Use Cases**: Creative writing, marketing content, executive summaries
- **Strengths**: More human-like, coherent summaries
- **Limitations**: Risk of hallucination, requires more training data

### 3. **Hybrid Summarization Agents**
- **Approach**: Combine extractive and abstractive methods
- **Key Techniques**: Multi-stage pipelines, reinforcement learning
- **Use Cases**: Technical documentation, medical reports, financial analysis
- **Strengths**: Balances accuracy and fluency
- **Limitations**: More complex implementation

## Key Capabilities to Look For

### **Core Functionalities**
- Multi-document summarization
- Domain adaptation (legal, medical, technical, etc.)
- Multi-language support
- Length-controlled summaries
- Keyphrase extraction
- Sentiment-aware summarization

### **Advanced Features**
- Query-focused summarization
- Update summarization (tracking changes over time)
- Factuality verification
- Citation preservation
- Structured output formats (JSON, XML, Markdown)
- API integration capabilities

## Available AI Agents (Based on Current Search)

### **1. arc42-documentation-writer**
- **Category**: Tech
- **Potential Relevance**: While focused on documentation writing, may include summarization capabilities for technical documents
- **Suggested Use**: Technical documentation summarization

### **2. ai-prompt-engineer**
- **Category**: Tech
- **Potential Relevance**: Can design effective prompts for LLM-based summarization
- **Suggested Use**: Prompt optimization for summarization tasks

### **3. ml-engineer**
- **Category**: Tech
- **Potential Relevance**: Can implement and fine-tune summarization models
- **Suggested Use**: Custom summarization model development

### **4. workflow-automation-engineer**
- **Category**: Tech
- **Potential Relevance**: Can automate summarization pipelines
- **Suggested Use**: End-to-end summarization workflows

## Learning Resources and Materials

### **Online Courses** (When course search is available, look for):
- Natural Language Processing Specializations
- Text Mining and Analytics
- Deep Learning for NLP
- Transformer Models in Practice

### **Key Research Papers**
1. **"Text Summarization with Pretrained Encoders"** - Liu et al. (2019)
2. **"BART: Denoising Sequence-to-Sequence Pre-training"** - Lewis et al. (2020)
3. **"PEGASUS: Pre-training with Extracted Gap-sentences for Abstractive Summarization"** - Zhang et al. (2020)
4. **"Long Document Summarization with Top-down and Bottom-up Inference"** - Zhong et al. (2020)

### **Practical Tools and Frameworks**
- **Hugging Face Transformers**: Pre-trained summarization models
- **spaCy**: Text processing pipeline

## 📝 三杯鸡经典配方与做法

*注：菜谱数据库暂时没有收录这道菜，以下是传统三杯鸡的标准配方，你可以对照检查家里的食材。*

### 🛒 所需食材清单

**主料：**
- 鸡腿肉 500g（或鸡翅中）
- 九层塔（罗勒叶） 1把（约30g）

**三杯调料（核心）：**
- 芝麻油 1杯（约240ml，实际用量约3-4汤匙）
- 酱油 1杯（约240ml，实际用量约3-4汤匙，可用生抽+老抽混合）
- 米酒 1杯（约240ml，实际用量约3-4汤匙，可用绍兴酒或台湾米酒）

**辅料：**
- 老姜 1大块（切片）
- 大蒜 8-10瓣（整粒或拍扁）
- 干辣椒 2-3个（可选）
- 冰糖或砂糖 1-2汤匙

### 👩‍🍳 制作步骤

1. **预处理：**
   - 鸡肉切块，用清水冲洗干净，沥干水分
   - 九层塔洗净，摘取叶子备用

2. **爆香：**
   - 锅中倒入芝麻油（比平时炒菜多些），中小火加热
   - 放入姜片，煎至边缘微卷、香气出来
   - 加入大蒜，炒至金黄色

3. **炒鸡：**
   - 转大火，放入鸡肉翻炒至表面变色
   - 加入干辣椒（如使用）翻炒均匀

4. **三杯调味：**
   - 沿锅边淋入米酒，让酒气挥发
   - 加入酱油，翻炒均匀上色
   - 加入冰糖/砂糖，翻炒至融化

5. **焖煮：**
   - 加入少量热水（约半杯），盖上锅盖
   - 中小火焖煮15-20分钟，至鸡肉熟透、汤汁收浓

6. **最后一步：**
   - 开大火收汁至浓稠
   - 关火，放入九层塔叶，用余温拌炒均匀
   - 出锅装盘

### 💡 小贴士
- **正宗三杯比例：** 麻油:酱油:米酒 = 1:1:1（但实际烹饪时可根据口味调整）
- **九层塔是关键：** 一定要最后放，才能保持香气
- **鸡肉选择：** 带皮鸡腿肉最嫩，鸡翅中也很适合
- **火候控制：** 先爆香姜蒜，再大火炒鸡，最后小火焖煮

- [ ] 芝麻油

```swift
import SwiftUI

struct WeatherView: View {
```

## Key SwiftUI Concepts Used:

1. **VStack/HStack**: For vertical and horizontal layouts
2. **LazyVGrid**: For responsive grid layouts
3. **Spacer()**: To push content to edges
4. **.padding()**: For proper spacing
5. **.background()**: With shapes for cards
6. **Image(systemName:)**: Using SF Symbols for icons
7. **.font()/.fontWeight()**: Typography hierarchy
8. **.foregroundColor()**: Color theming
9. **ScrollView**: For scrollable content

## Tips for Your Weather App:

1. Use **SF Symbols** for consistent icons (thermometer, humidity, wind, etc.)
2. Implement **dark mode support** using `.preferredColorScheme()` or system colors
3. Add **animations** for data updates with `.animation(.spring())`
4. Consider using **@State** and **@Binding** for dynamic data updates
5. Use **.refreshable** for pull-to-refresh functionality

These examples show different approaches - choose based on your app's design requirements. The grid layout works well for tablets, while the card layout is great for phones.

## Example 1: Simple Vertical Layout (VStack)

```swift
import SwiftUI

struct WeatherView: View {
    let temperature = 12.7
    let humidity = 69
    let windSpeed = 12.24
    let condition = "Clear sky"
    
    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 16) {
            Text("London")
                .font(.largeTitle)
                .fontWeight(.bold)
            
            Text(condition)
                .font(.title2)
                .foregroundColor(.secondary)
            
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 12) {
                WeatherRow(
                    icon: "thermometer",
                    label: "Temperature",
                    value: "\(temperature, specifier: "%.1f")°C"
                )
                
                WeatherRow(
                    icon: "humidity",
                    label: "Humidity", 
                    value: "\(humidity)%"
                )
                
                WeatherRow(
                    icon: "wind",
                    label: "Wind Speed",
                    value: "\(windSpeed, specifier: "%.1f") km/h"
                )
            }
        }
        .padding()
    }
}

struct WeatherRow: View {
    let icon: String
    let label: String
    let value: String
    
    var body: some View {
        HStack {
            Image(systemName: icon)
                .foregroundColor(.blue)
                .frame(width: 30)
            
            Text(label)
                .foregroundColor(.secondary)
            
            Spacer()
            
            Text(value)
                .fontWeight(.medium)
        }
    }
}
```

## Example 2: Horizontal Metric Cards (HStack)

```swift
struct WeatherCardsView: View {
    let temperature = 12.7
    let humidity = 69
    let windSpeed = 12.24

                icon: "wind",
                title: "Wind",
                value: "\(windSpeed, specifier: "%.1f") km/h",

            )
        }
        .padding(.horizontal)
    }
}

struct WeatherCard: View {
    let icon: String
    let title: String
    let value: String
    let color: Color
    
    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 12) {
            Image(systemName: icon)
```

## Key SwiftUI Concepts Used:

1. **VStack/HStack**: For vertical and horizontal layouts
2. **LazyVGrid**: For responsive grid layouts
3. **Spacer()**: To push content to edges
4. **.padding()**: For proper spacing
5. **.background()**: With shapes for cards
6. **Image(systemName:)**: Using SF Symbols for icons
7. **.font()/.fontWeight()**: Typography hierarchy
8. **.foregroundColor()**: Color theming
9. **ScrollView**: For scrollable content

## Tips for Your Weather App:

1. Use **SF Symbols** for consistent icons (thermometer, humidity, wind, etc.)
2. Implement **dark mode support** using `.preferredColorScheme()` or system colors
3. Add **animations** for data updates with `.animation(.spring())`
4. Consider using **@State** and **@Binding** for dynamic data updates
5. Use **.refreshable** for pull-to-refresh functionality

Introducing ActiveLife 3.0

We're excited to announce the release of ActiveLife 3.0, our biggest update yet for the fitness tracking app that helps users monitor their workouts, nutrition, and health metrics. This update brings a completely redesigned user interface built with SwiftUI, taking full advantage of the latest APIs available in iOS 17 and SwiftUI 5.

New Features at a Glance

ActiveLife 3.0 introduces several major enhancements:

  • Advanced Workout Analytics: Real-time performance metrics with interactive charts
  • Nutrition Planner 2.0: AI-powered meal suggestions based on fitness goals
  • Social Challenges: Compete with friends in weekly fitness challenges
  • HealthKit Integration: Deeper integration with Apple Health for comprehensive data tracking
  • WatchOS Companion: Redesigned Apple Watch app with new complications

SwiftUI: The Foundation of Our Redesign

We've completely rebuilt ActiveLife using SwiftUI, Apple's declarative UI framework. The migration from UIKit has allowed us to write more maintainable code, improve performance, and implement complex animations with significantly less code. One of the most impactful changes has been our adoption of SwiftUI's enhanced List APIs.

Leveraging SwiftUI's Latest List APIs

SwiftUI's List view has evolved dramatically since its introduction. In ActiveLife 3.0, we're using several advanced List features that were introduced in recent iOS versions:

1. Custom List Styles and Separators

We've implemented custom list appearances using the new .listStyle() modifier and separator controls:

List(workoutHistory) { workout in
    WorkoutRow(workout: workout)
}
.listStyle(.insetGrouped)
.listRowSeparator(.visible, edges: .all)
.listRowSeparatorTint(.blue.opacity(0.3))

This gives our workout history screen a distinctive look that aligns with our brand while maintaining native iOS feel.

2. Swipe Actions with Custom Icons

The new .swipeActions() modifier allows us to implement rich contextual actions:

List(mealPlanItems) { item in
    MealPlanRow(item: item)
        .swipeActions(edge: .trailing) {
            Button("Edit") { editItem(item) }
                .tint(.blue)
            Button("Delete", role: .destructive) { deleteItem(item) }
        }
        .swipeActions(edge: .leading) {
            Button("Favorite") { favoriteItem(item) }
                .tint(.yellow)
        }
}

Users can now quickly edit, delete, or favorite meal plan items with intuitive swipe gestures.

3. Searchable Lists with Scopes

We've implemented powerful search functionality using .searchable() with search scopes:

@State private var searchText = ""
@State private var searchScope = SearchScope.all

List(filteredWorkouts) { workout in
    WorkoutRow(workout: workout)
}
.searchable(text: $searchText, prompt: "Search workouts")
.searchScopes($searchScope) {
    Text("All").tag(SearchScope.all)
    Text("Running").tag(SearchScope.running)
    Text("Cycling").tag(SearchScope.cycling)
}

This allows users to quickly filter through hundreds of workouts by type and name.

4. Refreshable and Pagination

For social features, we implemented pull-to-refresh and infinite scrolling:

List(socialPosts) { post in
    SocialPostRow(post: post)
}
.refreshable {
    await loadNewPosts()
}
.onAppear {
    loadMoreContentIfNeeded()
}

The .refreshable() modifier provides native refresh behavior with minimal code.

5. List Row Backgrounds and Accents

We use .listRowBackground() and accent colors to highlight important metrics:

List(healthMetrics) { metric in
    HealthMetricRow(metric: metric)
        .listRowBackground(
            metric.isCritical ? Color.red.opacity(0.1) : Color.clear
        )
        .listRowSeparator(.hidden)
}

Critical health metrics are visually distinguished with subtle background tints.

Performance Improvements

The new List APIs aren't just about aesthetics—they also bring performance benefits. SwiftUI's List now uses lazy loading by default, and the new .id() modifier helps with efficient diffing when updating large datasets. We've seen a 40% reduction in memory usage for our workout history screen compared to our previous UIKit implementation.

Looking Ahead

We're just scratching the surface of what's possible with SwiftUI. As Apple continues to enhance the framework, we're excited to implement features like .scrollTargetBehavior for precise scrolling control and .scrollPosition for programmatic navigation.

Get Started with ActiveLife 3.0

ActiveLife 3.0 is available now on the App Store. For developers interested in our SwiftUI implementation, check out our open-source components on GitHub. We'll be sharing more technical deep dives in upcoming blog posts.

Want to learn more about SwiftUI List APIs? Visit the official Apple documentation for complete details and examples.

**Introducing LinguaLearn's Exciting New Features**

We're thrilled to announce the latest update to LinguaLearn, our comprehensive language learning application designed to make mastering new languages more accessible, engaging, and effective than ever before. **AI-Powered Conversation Practice**

One of our most significant additions is the AI Conversation Partner feature. Using advanced natural language processing, LinguaLearn now offers realistic, responsive dialogue practice that adapts to your proficiency level. Whether you're practicing casual greetings or complex business negotiations, our AI provides immediate feedback on pronunciation, grammar, and vocabulary usage.

This feature addresses a common challenge for language learners: finding consistent speaking practice opportunities. With our AI partner available 24/7, you can build confidence and fluency at your own pace.

**Personalized Learning Pathways**

Gone are the days of one-size-fits-all language courses. Our updated algorithm now creates customized learning pathways based on your goals, interests, and learning style. Whether you're preparing for travel, business, academic purposes, or personal enrichment, LinguaLearn tailors your curriculum accordingly.

The system continuously analyzes your performance, identifying strengths to reinforce and weaknesses to address, ensuring optimal progress toward your language objectives.

**Immersive Cultural Content**

Language learning extends beyond vocabulary and grammar—it's about understanding culture. Our new Cultural Immersion section features authentic media content, including short films, news clips, music videos, and podcasts from native-speaking countries. Each piece includes interactive transcripts, vocabulary highlights, and cultural notes.

This approach helps learners develop not just linguistic competence but also cultural awareness, preparing them for real-world interactions.

**Recent Trends in Language Learning Technology**

The language learning app landscape has evolved dramatically in recent years. Here are the key trends shaping the industry that we've incorporated into LinguaLearn's latest update:

**1. Microlearning Integration**
Modern learners increasingly prefer short, focused study sessions that fit into busy schedules. Research shows that consistent, brief practice sessions yield better retention than infrequent, lengthy study periods. LinguaLearn now features 5-10 minute "Quick Lessons" perfect for daily commutes, lunch breaks, or waiting periods.

**2. Gamification and Motivation Systems**
Effective language learning requires sustained motivation. Our updated achievement system, daily streaks, and interactive challenges transform learning into an engaging experience. Social features allow you to join study groups, participate in friendly competitions, and share progress with a supportive community.

**3. Voice Recognition Advancements**
Pronunciation practice has become more sophisticated with improved voice recognition technology. LinguaLearn's enhanced speech analysis provides detailed feedback on accent, intonation, and rhythm—crucial elements often overlooked in traditional language instruction.

**4. Cross-Platform Synchronization**
Seamless experience across devices is no longer a luxury but an expectation. LinguaLearn now offers instant synchronization between mobile, tablet, and web platforms, allowing learners to pick up exactly where they left off regardless of device.

**5. Data-Driven Personalization**
Advanced analytics enable increasingly personalized learning experiences. By leveraging machine learning, LinguaLearn identifies patterns in your learning behavior to optimize content delivery, review scheduling, and difficulty progression.

**What These Updates Mean for LinguaLearn Users**

Our commitment extends beyond implementing trends—we focus on how these innovations translate to tangible learning outcomes:

- **Faster Progress:** Personalized pathways and AI conversation practice accelerate language acquisition
- **Improved Retention:** Spaced repetition algorithms and microlearning techniques enhance long-term memory
- **Greater Engagement:** Gamified elements and cultural content maintain motivation throughout the learning journey
- **Real-World Readiness:** Practical conversation skills and cultural awareness prepare users for authentic interactions

**Looking Ahead**

This update represents just the beginning of our ongoing innovation journey. We're already exploring additional features, including virtual reality conversation scenarios, expanded language offerings, and deeper integration with real-world language use contexts.

answer:
**Perfect Dinner Party Menu for 6 (with Vegetarian & Gluten‑Free Accommodations)**

---

## 🍽️ **Three‑Course Menu**

### **STARTER**  
**Roasted Beetroot & Goat Cheese Tartlets**  
*Gluten‑free almond‑flour pastry, honey‑thyme glaze, micro‑greens*  
**Wine pairing:** **Sauvignon Blanc** – its bright acidity and citrus notes cut through the richness of the goat cheese and enhance the earthy beets.

---

### **MAIN**  
*Two options to satisfy all guests:*

1. **Slow‑Braised Beef Short Ribs**  
   *Red‑wine reduction, creamy polenta (gluten‑free), roasted seasonal vegetables*  

2. **Wild Mushroom & Lentil Wellington**  
   *Gluten‑free puff pastry, herb‑infused duxelles, red‑wine glaze*  
   *Suitable for both vegetarians and the gluten‑free guest*

**Wine pairing:** **Pinot Noir** – a versatile red with enough structure to stand up to the beef, yet delicate enough to complement the earthy mushrooms without overpowering them.

---

### **DESSERT**  
**Flourless Chocolate Torte**  
*Dark chocolate, almond meal, raspberry coulis, whipped cream*  
*Naturally gluten‑free and vegetarian*  
**Wine pairing:** **Late‑Harvest Riesling** or a **Ruby Port** – the sweetness and acidity balance the intense chocolate, while the port’s nutty notes echo the almond base.

---

## 🛒 **Shopping List (for 6)**  
*Proteins:* beef short ribs (4–5 lbs), goat cheese (8 oz), eggs, butter.  
*Produce:* beets (6 medium), mushrooms (1½ lbs), lentils (1 cup), onions, garlic, seasonal vegetables (carrots, zucchini, etc.), fresh herbs (thyme, rosemary), raspberries (for coulis).  
*Pantry:* almond flour (2 cups), gluten‑free all‑purpose flour (for pastry), polenta (1 cup), dark chocolate (12 oz), red wine (1 bottle for cooking + pairing), honey, olive oil, vegetable stock.  
*Dairy:* heavy cream, milk, Parmesan (for polenta).  
*Spices:* salt, pepper, smoked paprika, cinnamon.

---

## 🧪 **The Science Behind the Scenes**  
*(Great conversation starters for cocktails!)*

### **1. Why Slow‑Cooking Makes Meat Tender**  
The toughness of cheaper cuts comes from **collagen**, a fibrous protein that forms a network in connective tissues. When heated slowly (≈160°F/71°C) for several hours, collagen undergoes **thermal denaturation** and **hydrolysis**, breaking down into soluble **gelatin**. This gelatin lubricates the muscle fibers, resulting in a melt‑in‑your‑mouth texture.  

**Reference:** *Gevorkian et al., “Thermal (in)stability of type I collagen fibrils” (arXiv:0810.4172v1)* – this study shows how collagen’s mechanical properties change with temperature, explaining why low‑and‑slow heating is key to tenderization.

### **2. The Chemistry of Gluten‑Free Baking**  
Wheat flour contains **gluten**, a protein network that traps gas and gives dough elasticity and structure. Gluten‑free flours lack this network, so bakers must use **hydrocolloids** (xanthan gum, psyllium) or **gel‑forming agents** to mimic gluten’s viscoelasticity. These additives create a **polymer network** that holds moisture and provides the necessary “chew” and rise.

**Reference:** *Mao et al., “Normal force controlled rheology applied to agar gelation” (arXiv:1508.01689v3)* – while focused on agar gels, the paper illustrates how polymer gels form and how their rheological (flow) properties can be controlled, directly analogous to the binders used in gluten‑free baking.

---

## 🍷 **Wine‑Pairing Rationale**  
- **Sauvignon Blanc** with the starter: high acidity cleanses the palate of the creamy goat cheese.  
- **Pinot Noir** with the main: its moderate tannins and red‑fruit notes bridge the beef and mushroom dishes.  
- **Late‑Harvest Riesling/Port** with dessert: the sweetness matches the chocolate, while the wine’s acidity prevents cloying.

---

**Enjoy your dinner party!** With this menu, everyone—vegetarians, gluten‑avoiders, and omnivores alike—will feel thoughtfully included, and the science tidbits will add a layer of intellectual fun to the evening. Cheers! 🥂

**Perfect Dinner Party Menu for 6 (with Vegetarian & Gluten‑Free Accommodations)**

---

## 🍽️ **Three‑Course Menu**

### **STARTER**  
**Roasted Beetroot & Goat Cheese Tartlets**  
*Gluten‑free almond‑flour pastry, honey‑thyme glaze, micro‑greens*  
**Wine pairing:** **Sauvignon Blanc** – its bright acidity and citrus notes cut through the richness of the goat cheese and enhance the earthy beets.

---

### **MAIN**  
*Two options to satisfy all guests:*

1. **Slow‑Braised Beef Short Ribs**  
   *Red‑wine reduction, creamy polenta (gluten‑free), roasted seasonal vegetables*  

2. **Wild Mushroom & Lentil Wellington**  
   *Gluten‑free puff pastry, herb‑infused duxelles, red‑wine glaze*  
   *Suitable for both vegetarians and the gluten‑free guest*

**Wine pairing:** **Pinot Noir** – a versatile red with enough structure to stand up to the beef, yet delicate enough to complement the earthy mushrooms without overpowering them.

---

### **DESSERT**  
**Flourless Chocolate Torte**  
*Dark chocolate, almond meal, raspberry coulis, whipped cream*  
*Naturally gluten‑free and vegetarian*  
**Wine pairing:** **Late‑Harvest Riesling** or a **Ruby Port** – the sweetness and acidity balance the intense chocolate, while the port’s nutty notes echo the almond base.

---

## 🛒 **Shopping List (for 6)**  
*Proteins:* beef short ribs (4–5 lbs), goat cheese (8 oz), eggs, butter.  
*Produce:* beets (6 medium), mushrooms (1½ lbs), lentils (1 cup), onions, garlic, seasonal vegetables (carrots, zucchini, etc.), fresh herbs (thyme, rosemary), raspberries (for coulis).  
*Pantry:* almond flour (2 cups), gluten‑free all‑purpose flour (for pastry), polenta (1 cup), dark chocolate (12 oz), red wine (1 bottle for cooking + pairing), honey, olive oil, vegetable stock.  
*Dairy:* heavy cream, milk, Parmesan (for polenta).  
*Spices:* salt, pepper, smoked paprika, cinnamon.

---

## 🧪 **The Science Behind the Scenes**  
*(Great conversation starters for cocktails!)*

### **1. Why Slow‑Cooking Makes Meat Tender**  
The toughness of cheaper cuts comes from **collagen**, a fibrous protein that forms a network in connective tissues. When heated slowly (≈160°F/71°C) for several hours, collagen undergoes **thermal denaturation** and **hydrolysis**, breaking down into soluble **gelatin**. This gelatin lubricates the muscle fibers, resulting in a melt‑in‑your‑mouth texture.  

**Reference:** *Gevorkian et al., “Thermal (in)stability of type I collagen fibrils” (arXiv:0810.4172v1)* – this study shows how collagen’s mechanical properties change with temperature, explaining why low‑and‑slow heating is key to tenderization.

### **2. The Chemistry of Gluten‑Free Baking**  
Wheat flour contains **gluten**, a protein network that traps gas and gives dough elasticity and structure. Gluten‑free flours lack this network, so bakers must use **hydrocolloids** (xanthan gum, psyllium) or **gel‑forming agents** to mimic gluten’s viscoelasticity. These additives create a **polymer network** that holds moisture and provides the necessary “chew” and rise.

**Reference:** *Mao et al., “Normal force controlled rheology applied to agar gelation” (arXiv:1508.01689v3)* – while focused on agar gels, the paper illustrates how polymer gels form and how their rheological (flow) properties can be controlled, directly analogous to the binders used in gluten‑free baking.

---

## 🍷 **Wine‑Pairing Rationale**  
- **Sauvignon Blanc** with the starter: high acidity cleanses the palate of the creamy goat cheese.  
- **Pinot Noir** with the main: its moderate tannins and red‑fruit notes bridge the beef and mushroom dishes.  
- **Late‑Harvest Riesling/Port** with dessert: the sweetness matches the chocolate, while the wine’s acidity prevents cloying.

---

**Enjoy your dinner party!** With this menu, everyone—vegetarians, gluten‑avoiders, and omnivores alike—will feel thoughtfully included, and the science tidbits will add a layer of intellectual fun to the evening. Cheers! 🥂

**neuroresearch.org appears to be a parked/for-sale domain:**
